title: Microsoft Teams: Workflows template adds tag members to channels automatically
summary: The rollout dates, optional default and documented governance controls are supported. Licensing is cautiously described, but its classification should acknowledge the published Microsoft 365 standard-connector entitlement while preserving the uncertainty about this template's connectors.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans a Teams Workflows template for adding tag members to channels.
claims.quote: We are introducing the Join member to channel when user is added to tag template in the Workflows app to automatically add users to selected channels when they are added to a team tag.

claims.claim: The template is called Join member to channel when user is added to tag.
claims.quote: The Join member to channel when user is added to tag template will be available in the Workflows app.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Once configured, adding a user to the tag automatically adds that user to selected channels rather than requiring each channel addition to be performed manually.
claims.quote: Once configured, the workflow runs whenever a user is added to the tag, eliminating the need to add members to each channel manually.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes location-based and project-based groups with tags corresponding to sites, regions or projects as use cases.
claims.quote: This is especially useful for location-based or project-based groups where tags correspond to specific sites, regions, or projects, helping new members access relevant channels promptly.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The notice includes standard channels among channels all team members can access by default to which this template applies.
claims.quote: This applies to channels that all team members can access by default: standard channels and shared channels that are shared with everyone on the team.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The notice includes shared channels shared with everyone on the team in the template's documented channel scope.
claims.quote: This applies to channels that all team members can access by default: standard channels and shared channels that are shared with everyone on the team.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance; rationales: risk and impact
claims.claim: Nothing changes by default because the template is optional and does not run until someone in a team configures it.
claims.quote: Nothing changes by default. The template is optional and does not run until someone in a team configures it.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope: Who; Why it matters
claims.claim: Team owners can choose to configure the workflow, and affected users are those added to tags associated with configured workflows.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams users who are added to team tags associated with configured workflows.- Team owners who choose to configure the workflow.

claims.claim: The feature's default state is user-opt-in.
claims.quote: Nothing changes by default. The template is optional and does not run until someone in a team configures it.

claims.claim: Microsoft requires no administrator action and recommends reviewing Power Automate and Workflows policies if the organisation plans to use the template.
claims.quote: No action is required. If your organization plans to use this template, we recommend reviewing your Power Automate and Workflows policies to confirm that it is permitted.

claims.claim: The documented role for using the Teams admin center is Teams Administrator.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role. Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks but we recommend using the lower privilege role where possible.

claims.claim: The Workflows app must be enabled in the Teams admin center for the documented Workflows flow functionality to work.
claims.quote: The Workflows app must be enabled in the Microsoft Teams admin center in order for this functionality to work.

claims.claim: Blocking the Workflows app is an app-wide control rather than a switch for only this template.
claims.quote: As an admin, you control access to all types of agents and apps that are used across your organization. ... You can allow or block specific agents and apps on either the Manage apps page or in the app details page.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsTargetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ManageTagsPermissionMode <mode> updates tag-management permissions.

claims.claim: The Manage tags article says PowerShell cannot manage tags, in contrast with the cited policy cmdlet reference.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can control how tags are used across your organization in the Microsoft Teams admin center. You can’t use PowerShell to manage tags.

claims.claim: Team owners and team members with permission can manually create and assign tags.
claims.quote: Custom tags: Team owners and team members (if they have permissions) can manually create and assign tags to people based on attributes, such as role, project, skill, or location.

claims.claim: The Manage tags article describes Microsoft default as allowing both team owners and members.
claims.quote: If you haven't selected an option for Who can manage tags, the Microsoft default setting is used. Microsoft default is set to both team owners and members.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsTargetingPolicy reference equates MicrosoftDefault with EnabledTeamOwner.
claims.quote: Set this to MicrosoftDefault to user default setting in current Teams, which will be the same as EnabledTeamOwner.

claims.claim: In Teams for Education, non-owner students cannot manage tags when Who can manage tags is Team owners or Microsoft default.
claims.quote: If you're using Teams for Education, non-owner students can't manage tags when Who can manage tags is set to Team owners or Microsoft default.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: With Team owners can change who can manage tags enabled, Who can manage tags supplies each team's default and owners may change it.
claims.quote: When you turn on this setting, team owners can set whether team members can create and manage tags within a team and the value of the Who can manage tags setting is the default value for each team.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: With Team owners can change who can manage tags disabled, Who can manage tags cannot be changed per team.
claims.quote: If you turn off this setting, the Who can manage tags setting can’t be changed per team.
